sections.h2: Which sale route works for a Longview owner in a hurry?
sections.html:
Owners in Longview with a deadline generally choose between a listing, a private sale and a cash purchase that leaves the repairs to the buyer. A listing reaches the most buyers. A cash sale closes sooner when repairs, liens, tenants or an estate stand in the way.

The city is the seat of Gregg County, along Interstate 20 and U.S. highways 80 and 259, roughly 125 miles east of Dallas. It extends across the line into Harrison County, so the parcel's county decides which appraisal district and which clerk handle your paperwork.

  • Confirm the county from your deed or tax bill before you request offers.
  • Collect the deed, any mortgage payoff statement and the latest tax bill.
  • Set any cash offer beside the likely proceeds of a listing, minus repairs, commission and months of upkeep.

sections.h2: What does Longview's railroad and oilfield past mean for its houses?
sections.html:
Longview began in the early 1870s when the Southern Pacific, later the Texas and Pacific, extended track westward and platted a town a mile west of the older settlement of Earpville. The Handbook of Texas records incorporation on May 17, 1871, making it the first community in Gregg County to incorporate.

The East Texas oilfield discovery in the early 1930s kept Longview out of the worst of the Depression. The same entry says the population more than doubled in that decade, and postwar annexation of Greggton and Spring Hill pushed the total toward 62,762 by 1980.

That boom left a large stock of mid-century homes. Buyers inspecting them focus on roofs, foundations, old wiring and plumbing, so a seller of an older Longview house should expect repair requests.

sections.h2: Which industries and school districts shape demand in Longview?
sections.html:
The city grew from a cotton, lumber and railroad town into an industrial and medical center. The Handbook of Texas points to the Big Inch pipeline, which began at Longview in 1942 and carried crude oil east through 1945, a plant making earth-moving equipment, and a chemical complex that became the largest in inland Texas.

It also describes Longview, Pine Tree and Spring Hill independent school districts, each with a major high school, as serving the area when the entry was written. A buyer's school search often decides which neighborhoods get shown first, and the district also sets part of the tax bill.

Other postwar landmarks in the Handbook include Gregg County Airport, Lake Cherokee and the conversion of a wartime hospital complex into LeTourneau Technical Institute, and Texas Eastman came to a site near Longview in 1950. For decades the Kelly Plow Company, a farm-equipment factory open from 1882 until after World War II, was the main plant. The Handbook also notes a new county courthouse in 1932, paid for by oil-boom tax receipts.

Steady industrial and medical employers bring relocating workers, though demand follows oil and manufacturing cycles. A house in a sought-after district may sell on the open market, while one with deferred maintenance may suit a cash buyer.

sections.h2: Which office appraises a Longview house?
sections.html:
The Gregg County Appraisal District values real and business personal property in that county under the Texas Property Tax Code. Parcels on the Harrison side belong to that county's appraisal district, so check your tax statement for the office that applies.

Gregg's district announced a residential reappraisal running from July 2026 to March 2027, with exterior inspections and new photographs. Appraisers carry a pictured ID, a business card and a state registration card, and leave a door hanger and card when no one is home.

For a homestead exemption, the district lists three conditions: you hold title and use the home as your residence on the filing date, no spouse claims a residence homestead elsewhere, and you present a Texas license or state ID showing the same address. Its taxpayer liaison is at 4367 W Loop 281 in Longview, and the number it lists is 903-238-8823.

sections.h2: How does the Texas tax calendar play out for a Longview seller?
sections.html:
Longview owners follow the statewide calendar. Value and the tax lien are fixed on January 1, a protest deadline lands in mid-May, and bills go out about October 1. Late January is the last safe payment date for a Longview bill, and the Gregg district's reappraisal visits mean a new photo of your house may be on file by spring, and from February 1 a collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

  • School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value, with a further $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.
  • Disabled veterans receive tiered partial exemptions, and a 100 percent rating can mean a total exemption on the homestead.
  • Heirs missing from a recorded deed can submit an ownership affidavit to the district to claim the exemption.

At a sale, the title company divides the year's bill between buyer and seller. An open lien gets a payoff request and is cleared from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What can a Longview owner do about foreclosure or unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
Call the lender or tax office before a deadline, since both processes move on fixed steps. A Texas deed of trust lets a lender sell without a court, but only after a default notice with a twenty-day cure period and a sale notice three weeks ahead of an auction held early in a month.

Afterward, a lender may sue for a shortfall within two years. Redemption is narrow: for tax sales, a Texas Supreme Court opinion on the court system's site describes two years for homestead, farm or mineral property and 180 days for other land.

Closing a sale before the auction often leaves an owner better off than the auction price would. Have the payoff amounts and lien balances put in writing by the title company.

sections.h2: How are inherited and rented Longview houses handled?
sections.html:
Begin with the deed. Should the owner have passed away, work out whether probate is needed: a will can be probated for four years after death, and a muniment of title can pass real estate where the estate owes nothing beyond real-estate liens.

For a rented house, expect three days' written notice, a justice court filing, service on the tenant four days ahead of trial and a writ of possession six days after judgment. Because of that schedule, many owners sell while the renter is still living there.

sections.h2: Where does a Longview deed get recorded?
sections.html: The clerk of Gregg or Harrison County keeps the records, depending on where the land lies. The signature needs a notary's acknowledgment, and the clerk can quote current charges. Closing funds usually cover them. Longview owners should also check that the legal description matches the deed already of record.

faqs.q: Is a Longview house in Gregg or Harrison County?
faqs.a: Either, because the city crosses the county line. The appraisal district on your tax bill is the office to contact, and the clerk of that same county records the deed.

faqs.q: Can a lien stop a Longview sale?
faqs.a: No, though it must be paid. The title company requests payoff figures and settles liens from your proceeds, and a buyer cannot receive clear title while delinquent property taxes remain.

faqs.q: When are Longview property taxes late?
faqs.a: Most unpaid bills turn delinquent on February 1. A six percent penalty and one percent interest apply then, and the penalty grows monthly until July 1.

faqs.q: Must I repair a Longview house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer purchases as-is, with the price reflecting the work expected. Compare the offer against a repaired-and-listed price before deciding.

faqs.q: How quickly can foreclosure move in Texas?
faqs.a: Fast. A default notice gives twenty days to cure, a sale notice must come three weeks before the auction, and sales happen monthly. Talk to the lender early.
